key_insight: SkillFuzz treats skill composition itself as a fuzzing target, using planning-stage deviations from a baseline to uncover implicit intents that only appear when multiple benign skills interact.
engineering_relevance: This helps marketplace operators audit AI agent skills before execution, reducing the risk that reusable skills combine into unintended or harmful behaviors in deployed agent systems.
method: Extract structured skill contracts from marketplace skills
Use contract-guided Monte Carlo Tree Search to prioritize suspicious skill compositions
Compare planned intent against a skill-free baseline as a differential oracle
evidence_signal: On representative skill-marketplace workloads, SkillFuzz found over 1,000 distinct implicit intents under a fixed budget and validated more than 80% of the highest-risk flagged compositions during execution-time testing.
watch_item: The approach depends on the quality of extracted skill contracts and planning artifacts, so weak or incomplete skill documentation could reduce detection accuracy.
paper_title: SkillFuzz: Fuzzing Skill Composition for Implicit Intents Discovery in Open Skill Marketplaces
